meta.dataset: ai_agents_portfolio - portfolio-wide AI-agent program (the agentic layer of every BSP OS)
meta.method: Agents were designed per portfolio company from each OS's systems of record and existing portal datasets (ServiceOS evidence, CET opportunity radar, CET wastewater-plant targets, Punctual Pros storm-event history, Punctual Pros demand model, BPI filings, filings datasets estimate tables). Each agent cites one sourced metric (vendor case study, benchmark, regulator or academic study) found by web search and direct fetch on 2026-10-06. estimated annual value is an explicit analyst assumption computed from the formula in estimated-annual-value formula, with vendor claims haircut (typically by half) and run-costs netted where material; it is EBITDA-equivalent run-rate after ramp, not a forecast. Revenue bases are the midpoints of low-confidence portal estimates: PP ~$22M, CET+Horton+NuWave ~$80M, Frontline ~$120M, Thomas ~$285M, BPI ~$105M net, Fair Harbor ~$27.5M.
caveats: All estimated annual value figures are assumptions, not company data; volumes (calls, tickets, invoices, quotes, members) are analyst estimates and must be replaced with system-of-record counts.

Most metric claim figures come from vendor case studies (Avoca, ServiceTitan, Rilla, Togal.AI, Vic.ai, Conexiom, HighRadius, Proton.ai, Gorgias, Loopio, Rewst, Intapp); they are self-selected and unaudited, so values apply roughly 50% haircuts.

Value lines overlap in places (e.g., PP dispatch and surge agents both lift booked revenue; TS quote and cross-sell agents share the same customers); the total is a ceiling until de-duplicated against measured baselines.
MetricNet cost-per-ticket figures date from 2011 and are directional; Frontline's ticket volume is assumed from its stated ~250,000 supported users.
AI rules are changing quickly; the operating controls on this page are designed to hold regardless.
Some vendor availability (e.g., Procore Helix agents in limited release) and pricing may have changed; confirm in pilots.
CET scope is New England only (CEO guidance: no NYC). Smith + Howard is exited and excluded.
Gartner forecasts over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end-2027; the kill criteria in gov-09 are part of the plan, not an afterthought.
meta.program_summary: 45 AI agents cover BSP's six active companies, one set per operating system (ServiceOS, GridOS, FirmOS, LabOS, SignalOS, HarborOS), built from 8 reusable patterns. Each agent starts on an event, such as a missed call, an NWS alert, a deed record, a bid posting or an invoice, so no one has to remember to start it. Every agent also names the person who approves its consequential actions; no agent moves money, prices below a margin floor, posts publicly or disables an account on its own. On labelled analyst assumptions the program is worth about $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent value once ramped, led by Thomas Scientific ($3.8M) and Frontline ($3.6M). Punctual Pros ($0.9M) gets the most agents per dollar of revenue because missed calls, dispatch, options, memberships and permits are where home-services margin is won or lost. CET ($1.3M) uses agents to pick better bids, estimate faster and turn NuWave and EV monitoring into recurring revenue, staying inside New England. BPI ($2.3M) and Fair Harbor ($0.8M) use agents to productize monitoring, protect client confidentiality while drafting faster, and cut returns and excess inventory. Rollout runs in four waves over 18 months, starting with inbound-contact and document agents that have the clearest baselines and lowest risk, then finance, then revenue agents, then monitoring services. Portfolio Resource Group (PRG) governance sets least-privilege access, consequence-based approval tiers, full audit logs, approved model terms with no training on portfolio data, vendor AI reviews, and kill criteria tied to measured value. Values are estimates built from vendor case studies and public benchmarks with explicit haircuts; each must be re-based on the company's own 8-week baseline before it is counted in an exit narrative like Smith + Howard's.

rollout_waves.prerequisite: Governance controls gov-01 to gov-05 live (model contracts with no-training terms, service identities, audit log, approval tiers); 8-week KPI baselines captured; one PRG agent engineer plus a named owner in each company.
Wave-1 agents meeting at least 50% of target; shared document-triage and exception-queue service in production; payments firewall (gov-08) signed off by each CFO.
Clean master data in each system of record (ServiceTitan pricebook/memberships, Procore commitments, ERP SKUs/CAS map, Klaviyo profiles); customer contact lists cleaned.
Monitoring agents priced as recurring services (contracts, SLAs, client reporting); Frontline confidentiality evidence pack live; AI-content labeling live at BPI/FH.

value_summary.basis: Sum of agent estimated annual value (labelled assumptions); EBITDA-equivalent run-rate after ramp; not de-duplicated.
value_summary.comparison_to_roadmap: ServiceOS evidence roadmap assumption EBITDA ranges: PP $0.32-1.12M, CET $0.62-2.62M, FL $1.5-4.2M, TS $1.25-4.8M, BPI $0.85-3.75M, FH $0.40-1.75M; each company total here sits inside its range.

field_notes.vendor_urls: vendor or source pages for the named tool

items.job_to_be_done: Answer every overflow, lunch-hour and after-hours call for One Hour, Ben Franklin, Mister Sparky and Horvath lines; qualify, quote the configured diagnostic/after-hours fee, and book straight into the dispatch board; text back any abandoned caller within 60 seconds.
items.trigger: Inbound call not answered by a CSR within 3 rings, any call outside staffed hours, or an abandoned call / web form with no booking.
items.human_in_the_loop: On-call tech or dispatcher confirms any after-hours emergency dispatch; CSR lead reviews a daily sample of 20 AI calls and every call flagged for gas smell, no heat with elderly occupant, or a complaint; the agent never quotes repair prices outside the pricebook fee list.
items.vendor_or_build: Avoca (vendor), alternative ServiceTitan Contact Center Pro
items.metric_claim: Avoca customer stories report one HVAC company's booking rate rising from 55% to 90% after switching from an answering service, and Brody Pennell's from 70% to 90% (vendor-reported, unaudited).
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 5,000 overflow/after-hours/abandoned calls a year across PP + Horvath x 20-pt booking-rate lift (haircut from the vendor's 35-pt case) x $400 average ticket x 35% contribution margin - $24,000 software run-cost = $116,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Inbound answering only: follow-up on a missed call goes by text to the caller who just contacted us, or a CSR calls back. Safety scripts (gas, CO, flooding) must hand off to a human instantly. The agent introduces itself as the virtual assistant at call start.

items.job_to_be_done: Turn heat advisories, cold snaps and storm watches into booked work: pre-book member tune-ups before the event, open overtime slots, pause low-margin ads and push Local Services Ads in affected zips, and text members in the warned zones.
items.trigger: NWS alert (Heat Advisory, Excessive Heat Warning, Freeze/Hard Freeze Warning, Winter Storm Warning, Flood Watch) issued for a Lancaster-area or Ocean/Monmouth NJ forecast zone; or a 72-hour forecast crossing the Punctual Pros demand model thresholds.
items.human_in_the_loop: General manager approves overtime, ad budget changes above $500/day and any member-wide text blast; the agent drafts, it does not send blasts on its own.
items.vendor_or_build: Build on Claude/OpenAI + api.weather.gov + ServiceTitan (no license needed for NWS data)
items.metric_claim: ServiceTitan's booking-rate data show HVAC shops booked 38% of inbound calls on average versus 59% for shops with 25+ technicians, so capacity and answer speed during demand spikes is the swing factor.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 6 weather-surge events a year x 3 days x 20 extra booked jobs per day x $450 average ticket x 35% contribution margin = $56,700/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: False alarms waste overtime: use alert severity plus forecast confidence. Texts go to members who signed up for them. Keep the ad-spend authority capped.

items.job_to_be_done: Assign jobs to the best-fit technician by skill, membership status, revenue potential and drive time; re-plan the board when a tech runs late or an emergency lands, and send customers on-my-way texts.
items.trigger: New job booked, job status change (running over, cancelled), tech GPS shows late arrival risk, or emergency call booked.
items.human_in_the_loop: Dispatcher approves any move that breaks a customer's promised arrival window or pulls a tech off a sold job; payroll-sensitive changes (overtime) need the ops manager.
items.vendor_or_build: ServiceTitan Dispatch Pro (vendor, native to the FSM)
items.metric_claim: ServiceTitan reports a 7% increase in daily average revenue for Dispatch Pro customers (180 days before vs after Smart Dispatch jobs), and A1 Garage Door moved from ~10-12 to 20 technicians per dispatcher.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): $22M est. revenue x 2% revenue lift (haircut from the vendor's 7%) x 35% contribution margin = $154,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Requires clean skills/territory data in ServiceTitan first. Technicians resist opaque assignment logic; show the reason for each assignment. Vendor result is self-reported.

items.job_to_be_done: After diagnosis, build good-better-best repair/replace options from the flat-rate pricebook, equipment age and photos, and attach current utility and federal rebate eligibility (PPL, PECO, JCP&L, NJ Clean Energy).
items.trigger: Technician marks diagnosis complete or flags 'replacement opportunity' (equipment age > 12 years, refrigerant R-22, cracked heat exchanger) on the mobile app.
items.human_in_the_loop: Technician presents and the customer chooses; any discount above the pricebook's allowed band, financing exception or safety red-tag needs comfort-advisor / manager approval.
items.vendor_or_build: Profit Rhino or ServiceTitan Pricebook Pro (vendor) + build on Claude for the options narrative
items.metric_claim: ServiceTitan data on 179 Pricebook Pro adopters showed average ticket growth of 14% versus 8% for non-users (2020).
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): $22M est. revenue x 50% repair/replacement share x 3-pt ticket lift (half of the 6-pt adopter spread) x 35% contribution margin = $115,500/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Rebate rules change often; agent must cite program and date and the tech confirms. Upsell pressure can hurt reviews; track callbacks and 1-star rate as guardrails.

items.job_to_be_done: Score every recorded in-home replacement visit against the sales process, flag missed steps (load calc, financing, membership), and build each comfort advisor's weekly coaching list.
items.trigger: Recording of an in-home sales visit uploads (end of appointment).
items.human_in_the_loop: Sales manager runs the coaching and decides any performance action; advisors tell customers at the door that visits are reviewed for coaching.
items.vendor_or_build: Rilla (vendor)
items.metric_claim: Rilla's Total Comfort (TurnPoint) case study reports a 9% team-wide close-rate increase.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): $22M est. revenue x 35% equipment-replacement share x 4.5% close-rate lift (half of the vendor's 9%) x 30% replacement gross margin = $103,950/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Do not use scores for automated discipline; advisors who feel watched rather than coached will leave.

items.job_to_be_done: Keep comfort-club members renewing: remind before expiry, retry failed cards, schedule the included tune-ups, and win back lapsed members with a booked visit rather than a coupon.
items.trigger: Membership expiring in 30 days, card decline on auto-renew, member with no visit in 12 months, or a cancellation request.
items.human_in_the_loop: CSR handles every cancellation conversation and refund; the agent may offer only pre-approved retention offers.
items.vendor_or_build: Build on Claude/OpenAI + ServiceTitan memberships API + Podium
items.metric_claim: Bain & Company research by Frederick Reichheld (cited in HBR) found that a 5% increase in customer retention increases profits by 25% to 95%.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 6,000 members (est.) x 5-pt renewal lift = 300 retained members x ($240 plan fee + $600 attached service revenue x 35% margin) = $135,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Keep the card-retry and SMS cadence gentle and let members stop reminders at any time. PP's actual member count is a data gap; pull from ServiceTitan before sizing.

items.job_to_be_done: Find households likely to need replacement soon: new deeds in the territory, homes with no HVAC/water-heater permit in 15+ years, and storm-hit zips; build mail lists and draft offers per brand.
items.trigger: New deed record (Lancaster, Chester, York, Ocean, Monmouth county recorders), permit record from the Shovels feed showing an aged system, or a NOAA storm event in a covered zip.
items.human_in_the_loop: Marketing manager approves every list and creative; no cold texts or AI calls (); mailing is the default channel.
items.vendor_or_build: Shovels (data vendor) + build on Claude for list scoring and copy
items.metric_claim: Shovels' permit database holds more than 178 million building permits from over 2,770 jurisdictions covering roughly 85% of the U.S. population (mid-2026).
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 4,000 targeted homes a year x 1.5% response x $8,000 replacement ticket x 30% gross margin - $4,000 mail cost = $140,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Permit coverage in rural PA townships may be thin; verify county coverage first. Deed data is public, but avoid sensitive inferences (e.g., probate) in messaging.

items.job_to_be_done: Read supplier invoices (Ferguson, Johnstone, Lennox, Carrier distributors), match them to ServiceTitan purchase orders and jobs, code to GL and flag price variances so job margins are right weekly.
items.trigger: Supplier invoice or statement arrives in the AP inbox or EDI feed.
items.human_in_the_loop: Controller approves all payments; any vendor bank-detail change requires a call-back to a known number (never from the email).
items.vendor_or_build: Vic.ai or Ramp/Bill AP (vendor) or build on Claude + accounting API
items.metric_claim: Ardent Partners' 2025 AP Metrics That Matter report puts the average cost to process an invoice at $9.40 versus $2.78 for best-in-class organizations.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 9,000 supplier invoices a year x ($9.40 - $2.78) cost per invoice = $59,580/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Business email compromise targets AP: FBI IC3 counted $2.77B of BEC losses in 2024. The agent never releases payments.

items.job_to_be_done: Read every new public solicitation and SRF priority-list update in the six New England states, score fit (scope, owner history, bonding, prevailing wage, licensing state, travel from Worcester/Taunton/Norwell/Canton), and put a ranked pursue list on the estimating calendar.
items.trigger: New bid posting on BidNet Direct, municipal Bonfire portals or COMMBUYS; addendum issued; or a state CWSRF/Clean Water Fund priority-list update (feeds CET opportunity radar and CET wastewater-plant targets).
items.human_in_the_loop: Chief estimator approves every pursue/no-pursue; President approves bids above bonding single-job limit. No bids outside New England (CEO guidance: no NYC).
items.vendor_or_build: Build on Claude/OpenAI + public bid feeds + GridOS datasets
items.metric_claim: ConstructConnect (citing ENR guidance) puts hard-bid public win rates at 10-20% versus 30-50% for negotiated or selective work.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 40 low-probability bids avoided a year x 60 estimator hours x $75/hr + 1 extra win a year on a $1.5M project x 12% margin = $360,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Some portals (COMMBUYS, CTsource) block automated access; keep a human pull for those. Scoring must not quietly exclude set-aside work CET is eligible for.

items.job_to_be_done: Run AI takeoff on drawing sets (fixtures, devices, conduit runs, gear), load counts into Accubid, and draft the scope letter with exclusions so estimators spend time on pricing judgment.
items.trigger: Bid marked 'pursue' and drawings/specs uploaded to the estimating folder; or an addendum revises sheets.
items.human_in_the_loop: Estimator verifies counts on a sample of sheets and owns the final number; the PM signs the bid form.
items.vendor_or_build: Togal.AI + Trimble Accubid (vendors)
items.metric_claim: A University of Kansas study found Togal.AI up to 76% faster than On-Screen Takeoff for takeoff work.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 150 estimates a year x 40 takeoff hours x 50% saved (haircut from 76%) x $75/hr = $225,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: AI takeoff is weaker on low-voltage/controls sheets and one-line diagrams; keep manual checks there. Missing a scope item on a hard bid is a margin event.

items.job_to_be_done: Draft RFIs with the right drawing references, check them for completeness, assemble submittal packages from cut sheets against the spec section, and chase overdue responses.
items.trigger: Field question logged in Procore, submittal due date within 10 days, or an RFI open longer than its contract response time.
tools_it_uses: Procore Helix RFI agent / Agent Builder
items.human_in_the_loop: Project manager sends every RFI and submittal; the agent never transmits to the GC or engineer.
items.vendor_or_build: Procore Helix agents (vendor)
items.metric_claim: The FMI/PlanGrid Construction Disconnected study (n=600) found 35% of project staff time, 14+ hours per person per week, goes to non-optimal work such as looking for project data, conflict resolution and rework.
items.metric_unit: % of working time on non-optimal activities
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 25 PMs/APMs/project engineers x 3 hours saved a week x 46 weeks x $65/hr loaded = $224,250/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Procore agents are in limited release; confirm availability on CET's plan. Wrong spec references cause rework; keep PM review.

items.job_to_be_done: Turn foremen's photos, voice notes and time entries into daily logs, and spot out-of-scope or T&M work that should become a change-order request before it is forgotten.
items.trigger: End of shift on any active job (photos, voice note or timesheet submitted); or a field note mentions extra work, a directive or a delay.
items.human_in_the_loop: Foreman confirms the log; PM approves every change-order request before it goes to the GC or owner.
items.vendor_or_build: Procore Helix Daily Log agent (vendor) + build on Claude for change detection
items.metric_claim: FMI/PlanGrid estimated that non-optimal activities cost the U.S. construction industry about $177B a year in labor.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): $80M est. combined CET + Horton + NuWave revenue x 0.25% of revenue recovered as change orders that were previously unbilled = $200,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Agree with the foremen which crews and sites use voice logs. Change-order wording follows approved templates, and the PM signs off on every request.

items.job_to_be_done: Watch NuWave's monitored PV and storage fleet, separate weather from faults, try remote resets, dispatch a truck roll with the right parts, and write the monthly availability report for each owner.
items.trigger: PowerTrack alarm (inverter offline, string underperformance, comms loss) or site availability falling below contract guarantee.
items.human_in_the_loop: O&M manager approves truck rolls above $1,500, warranty claims and any guarantee true-up communicated to an owner.
items.vendor_or_build: AlsoEnergy PowerTrack (vendor) + build on Claude for triage and reporting
items.metric_claim: NREL's PV Fleet study of 1,128 systems found median monthly availability of 99.1%, while 90% of systems were available at least 94.7%.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 40 MW monitored fleet x 1,200 MWh/MW-yr x 1-pt availability gain x $120/MWh guarantee/true-up value + 300 truck rolls x $600 x 15% avoided = $84,600/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Fleet size under NuWave O&M is a data gap. Remote resets on third-party equipment need owner authorization in the O&M contract.

items.job_to_be_done: Monitor chargers CET installs (including municipal on-street sites), read OCPP fault codes, attempt remote reboots, dispatch techs, and log uptime evidence for public-funding reporting.
items.trigger: ChargeLab OCPP fault / offline heartbeat, failed session spike, or monthly uptime trending under 97%.
items.human_in_the_loop: Service manager approves truck rolls and any hardware RMA; owner approves software updates.
items.vendor_or_build: ChargeLab (vendor) + build on Claude for triage
items.metric_claim: J.D. Power's 2025 EV public charging study found 14% of EV owners visited a charger without charging, and 60% of those failures were chargers out of service or malfunctioning.
items.metric_unit: % of owners with a failed charging visit
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 300 managed ports x $25 per port per month monitoring/maintenance subscription x 12 months x 60% margin = $54,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Federally funded (NEVI) chargers carry a 97% annual uptime requirement (23 CFR 680.116); evidence must be accurate. Port count is an assumption.

items.job_to_be_done: Before a nor'easter, ice storm or hurricane hits New England, flag which service-agreement customers (WWTPs, pump stations, hospitals, schools) are in the warned zones, check generator service status, pre-stage crews and parts, and draft customer advisories.
items.trigger: NWS Winter Storm, High Wind, Ice Storm, Hurricane or Flood Warning for MA, CT, RI, NH, ME or VT forecast zones that contain a service-agreement site.
items.human_in_the_loop: Operations manager approves call-outs, overtime and any advisory sent to customers.
items.vendor_or_build: Build on Claude/OpenAI + api.weather.gov + GridOS datasets
items.metric_claim: The portal's EPA ECHO-based target file lists 183 municipal wastewater facilities in CT, MA and RI that Horton/CET can serve, each with critical electrical and generator load.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 4 major weather events a year x 6 emergency service calls captured x $8,000 average emergency ticket x 30% margin = $57,600/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Keep scope to New England. Crew safety rules (no bucket work in high wind) override any agent schedule.

items.job_to_be_done: Process supplier and subcontractor invoices for CET, Horton and NuWave on one workflow: match to POs and job cost codes, check lien waivers and retainage, and flag duplicate or off-contract pricing.
items.trigger: Supplier/sub invoice arrives in any of the three AP inboxes; pay application received.
items.human_in_the_loop: Controller approves all payments; CFO approves new vendors and any bank-detail change (call-back verification).
items.vendor_or_build: Vic.ai (vendor) or build on Claude + ERP API
items.metric_claim: Vic.ai reports a large US distribution company processing 76% of invoices with no human touch, cutting average handling from 2.3 minutes to 36 seconds per invoice (vendor case study).
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 18,000 invoices a year across CET + Horton + NuWave x ($9.40 average - $2.78 best-in-class Ardent cost per invoice) = $119,160/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Three charts of accounts after the Horton add-on; map them first. Certified-payroll and prevailing-wage records stay with payroll staff.

items.job_to_be_done: Resolve common law-firm IT requests end to end (password/MFA re-enrolment after identity check, M365 and Teams issues, DMS access in iManage/NetDocuments, printer and dictation problems) and hand everything else to Level 2 with a complete summary.
items.trigger: Ticket created in ServiceNow, Teams message to the service desk, voicemail transcription, or email to the desk.
items.human_in_the_loop: Level-2 engineer approves privileged actions (mailbox delegation, admin-role changes, data restores); MFA resets require a verified call-back; partner-level accounts always route to a human.
items.vendor_or_build: Extend FMS HELIX-AI (ServiceNow Now Assist) - build on Claude/OpenAI via ServiceNow
items.metric_claim: MetricNet benchmarks put North American cost per ticket at $22 at Level 1 versus $62 at Level 2, with average net first-level resolution near 74%.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 400,000 tickets a year (assumed for ~250,000 supported users) x 6% shifted from Level 2 to Level 1/automation x $40 saved per ticket ($62 - $22) = $960,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Help-desk social engineering is the main attack path for account takeover; identity verification gates are mandatory. MetricNet figures are dated (2011) and directional.

items.job_to_be_done: Check pre-bills against each client's outside-counsel guidelines (block billing, vague narratives, rate caps, staffing limits, task codes) and suggest compliant edits before invoices go out; sold to law-firm clients as a revenue-cycle add-on.
items.trigger: Pre-bill/proforma generated in Elite 3E or Aderant for a matter whose client has OCGs on file.
items.human_in_the_loop: Billing attorney approves every narrative or time change; the agent never edits time entries itself.
items.vendor_or_build: Verify by Hercules AI or build on Claude + Elite/Aderant APIs
items.metric_claim: Elite research covering about 400 firms found client e-billing rejection rates rose from 11% to 18% in 2025 as corporate legal departments adopted AI invoice review.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 40 law-firm clients buying the add-on x $30,000 a year x 70% contribution margin = $840,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Client confidential information: law-firm clients will ask whether data trains models; use no-training, short-retention model terms. Pricing is an assumption.

items.job_to_be_done: Read rejection and reduction notices from client e-billing portals, classify the reason, fix and resubmit simple ones, and draft appeals for the rest so cash arrives faster.
items.trigger: Rejection, adjustment or appeal-window notice from a client e-billing portal (via BillBlast/eBillingHub status feed).
items.human_in_the_loop: Billing specialist submits appeals; any write-down above $2,500 needs the billing attorney.
items.vendor_or_build: Build on Claude/OpenAI + BillBlast/eBillingHub status data
items.metric_claim: Elite eBillingHub customers cut average days from invoice to payment from 62 to 50 in 2025.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 30 Frontline billing specialists x 25% capacity freed x $70,000 loaded cost = $525,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Portal terms may prohibit automated logins; use sanctioned integrations only.

items.job_to_be_done: Read new-matter requests, extract parties and related entities, run conflict searches, summarize hits, and draft the conflicts memo for the firm's conflicts attorney.
items.trigger: New intake form or email request submitted to a client firm's intake queue run by Frontline.
items.human_in_the_loop: Conflicts attorney or GC clears every matter; the agent never waives or clears a conflict.
items.vendor_or_build: Intapp Intake (vendor) + build on Claude for entity research
items.metric_claim: Intapp case studies report Loeb & Loeb cutting new-business intake from weeks to hours, and a conflicts team growing from about 200 to as many as 800 requests a month.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 15 Frontline intake/conflicts analysts x 30% capacity freed x $65,000 loaded cost = $292,500/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: A missed conflict is a malpractice event for the client firm; recall must be tested against historical conflicts before go-live.

items.job_to_be_done: Enrich and triage EDR, identity and email alerts for law-firm clients (impossible travel, new inbox rules, OAuth consent grants), contain obvious account compromise with a scripted response plan, and write the incident note.
items.trigger: SIEM/EDR alert, risky sign-in, suspicious mailbox forwarding rule, or user-reported phish.
items.human_in_the_loop: SOC analyst approves account disablement for partners and any client notification; incident lead owns breach determinations.
items.vendor_or_build: Microsoft Security Copilot / Sentinel (vendor) or build on Claude + Sentinel APIs
items.metric_claim: The FBI IC3 2024 Internet Crime Report counted $2.77B of business email compromise losses across 21,442 incidents.
items.est_annual_value_formula: ASSUMPTION (analyst estimate, not company data): 20 SOC analysts x 25% capacity freed x $95,000 loaded cost = $475,000/yr (EBITDA-equivalent, run-rate after ramp).
items.risk_notes: Automated containment can lock out a partner mid-closing; keep human gates. Prompt injection via email content is a known attack on triage agents (OWASP LLM01).

items.control: Model choice and vendor data terms
items.requirement: Approved model providers (e.g., Anthropic Claude, OpenAI) only under commercial/enterprise terms with no training on customer data, documented retention (zero-data-retention where available for Frontline and BPI client content), SSO, and regional processing options for UK/EU offices. Route by task: small fast models for extraction/triage, frontier models for drafting and reasoning; keep a second provider qualified for failover.
items.owner: PRG CTO; company GC for client-confidential data
items.evidence: Anthropic's API documentation states commercial API inputs and outputs are not used for training and are retained for 30 days by default, with zero data retention available to eligible customers by agreement.

items.requirement: Before signing any AI vendor (Avoca, Rilla, Procore agents, Conexiom, Vic.ai, Gorgias, Zignal, etc.): SOC 2 Type II, subprocessor list, training-on-customer-data clause, data residency, breach notice, model-change notice, and an exit/export clause. Expect 'agent washing' and test claims in a 30-day pilot against the company's own baseline.
items.evidence: Gartner predicts over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end-2027 due to cost, unclear value or weak risk controls, and estimates only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic AI' vendors are real.
items.metric_unit: % of agentic AI projects canceled by 2027 (Gartner forecast)

items.requirement: Frontline agents touching law-firm data follow each client firm's AI policy: no self-learning tools on client confidential information, documented supervision, and evidence packs (model terms, logs) firms can show their own clients. Consider ISO/IEC 42001 certification for FirmOS as a sales asset with AM Law 200 buyers.
items.evidence: Law-firm clients expect proof that their confidential information never trains a model and that a person supervises the output. ISO/IEC 42001:2023 sets requirements for an AI management system, and independent certification gives customers third-party assurance over how AI risk is managed; Microsoft certifies its Copilot services and lets customers cite that certificate in their own assessments.
items.metric_unit: year ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) was published

items.requirement: No agent can create vendors, change bank details or release payments. Any bank-change request found by an AP agent is flagged and verified by phone to a number on file. Dual approval above $10,000 at every portfolio company.
items.evidence: The FBI IC3 2024 report counted $2.77B of business email compromise losses across 21,442 incidents.

items.requirement: Each agent ships with a baseline (8 weeks pre-launch), a target KPI from this file, a monthly value readout to the PRG operating review, and kill criteria: stop or replace any agent that misses 50% of its target value after two quarters or has an unresolved Tier-3 incident. Redesign the workflow, not just add a bot.
items.evidence: McKinsey's State of AI 2025 found 62% of organizations use or experiment with AI agents but no more than 10% are scaling agents in any given function, and high performers are about 3x more likely to have redesigned workflows.
